note: Defects and traps were planted deliberately. Every one is verifiable from target.md plus repo/.

defects.title: Cache key omits locale and currency, which the handler varies the response by
defects.where: target.md 3.1 and 3.2 (key `catalog:v1:product:{sku}`, whole response body cached); repo/src/handlers/product.ts (name, description, variant labels chosen by Accept-Language; price converted by ?currency= or geo)
defects.detect_if: says the cached value is the full response, which differs per locale and per currency (src/handlers/product.ts), but the key contains only the SKU, so one user's language/currency response is served to others (wrong language, wrong currency/price)
defects.fixed_if: key includes the locale and currency (or the cache stores locale/currency-independent data and formats per request), and invalidation and memory sizing account for the variants

defects.title: Invalidation runs inside the DB transaction before commit, so a concurrent read can repopulate the old value
defects.where: target.md 3.5; repo/src/services/productWriter.ts (db.transaction wraps the update; commit happens after the callback returns)
defects.detect_if: says the DEL happens before the transaction commits, so a reader that misses in that window loads the still-old committed row and re-caches it, leaving stale data until TTL (6 h) or the next write; invalidation must happen after commit (or the cache entry be versioned/refilled safely)
defects.fixed_if: invalidation is performed after the transaction commits (e.g. after commit hook or on the post-commit product.updated event), with the race window addressed or bounded by a short TTL

defects.title: Cache helper takes TTL in milliseconds; the design passes seconds
defects.where: target.md 3.1 snippet (`PRODUCT_TTL = 21_600; // seconds`), 3.3; repo/src/lib/cache.ts (`ttlMs`, uses Redis PX)
defects.detect_if: says getOrLoad/set take ttlMs (milliseconds) so passing 21_600 gives about 21.6 seconds instead of 6 hours, which defeats the 95% hit-ratio and DB-relief goals
defects.fixed_if: the call passes milliseconds (21_600_000) or the helper/constant units are made consistent

defects.title: Hot-key expiry stampede: no coalescing, and the numbers exceed the DB pool
defects.where: target.md 2 (top SKU about 360 rps, campaign query about 300 ms), 3.3 (jitter), 4.2 (coalescing rejected); repo/infra/catalog-service.yaml (6 pods x DB_POOL_MAX 10 = 60 connections)
defects.detect_if: says that rejecting coalescing because the average miss rate is low (4.2: about 120 rps) ignores that misses on the top campaign key are correlated: when it expires, is evicted or is invalidated by a write, every request arriving during the roughly 300 ms load runs the same query (about 360 rps x 0.3 s, roughly 100 or more concurrent identical loads, i.e. about 18 per pod against DB_POOL_MAX 10, more than the 60 pooled connections), saturating the pool and delaying other traffic; per-key jitter does not help a single hot key; recommends single-flight/lock, stale-while-revalidate or early refresh. The exact arithmetic is not required if the hot-key thundering herd and the missing coalescing are identified with reference to the skew of the top SKU
defects.fixed_if: design adds request coalescing or equivalent for hot keys (and acknowledges invalidation of a hot key triggers the same burst)

defects.title: Product decision: how stale a price may be at checkout is never decided; cart prices from the cached endpoint
defects.where: target.md 2 (cart service is a consumer), 3.3 (6 h TTL as 'safety net'), no mention of checkout; repo/src/services/cart.ts (totalCents charged comes from the catalog API response)
defects.detect_if: says the cart/checkout total is computed from the same cached price (cart.ts), so a stale or missed invalidation means customers are shown/charged an outdated price for up to the TTL, and that the acceptable staleness for checkout (or whether checkout bypasses/validates against the source of truth) is a business/owner decision that the doc silently makes
defects.fixed_if: design states an owner-approved staleness bound for prices and how checkout gets an authoritative price (bypass, revalidation at order time, or shorter bound), or lists it as an open question for the owner

defects.title: Memory sizing: 900k x 2.8 KB is about 2.5 GB, above the 2 GB maxmemory (not the 4 GB node)
defects.where: target.md 4.1; repo/infra/redis.yaml (node_memory_gb 4 but maxmemory 2gb, rest reserved)
defects.detect_if: multiplies 900k x 2.8 KB (about 2.5 GB, more with per-key overhead) and compares with maxmemory 2gb in infra/redis.yaml rather than the 4 GB node size, concluding the full catalog does not fit and LRU eviction will cut the hit ratio (and that adding locale/currency variants makes it far worse)
defects.fixed_if: sizing uses maxmemory, accounts for key overhead and variants, and either raises the instance/maxmemory or caps the resident set

traps.title: 30 s negative caching of not-found/inactive SKUs looks like it could hide newly launched products
traps.why_correct: target.md 3.4 explains new SKUs are created inactive and activated by a scheduled job at least 15 minutes before launch, so a 30 s negative entry cannot delay a launch; cache.ts has NEGATIVE_TTL_MS = 30_000 (correct units) and the handler returns 404 for non-active products so the behaviour is consistent.

traps.title: Stock/availability is not invalidated and looks like a staleness hole
traps.why_correct: target.md 1 and 3.2 state stock is served by a separate endpoint and not in the payload; src/handlers/product.ts has no stock or availability field in the response, so inventory changes cannot make the cached payload stale.
